beats: Hook: a skip connection is one express lane past every block; what if you built four, and how do you keep them from blowing up? (line_res_bypass_road, line_res_four_lanes)
Why the skip path: with x + F(x), layer 100's gradient reaches layer 1 directly; without it the signal is a whisper passed through 100 people (line_whisper_line, line_res_bypass_road).
LayerNorm, not BatchNorm: sequences differ in length, so normalise each token on its own, not across the batch (slide 23) (line_res_tailor_split).
RMSNorm: drop the mean and the bias, about as good and cheaper; Llama-family models use it (slide 24).

Post-LN vs Pre-LN: a toll gate across the highway vs a gate on the exit ramp only; Pre-LN leaves the identity path clean, only early models like BERT kept Post-LN (slide 25) (line_res_gate_on_road, line_res_gate_on_ramp).
Peri-LN: gates on the way in and out of the ramp, highway untouched (Gemma 2/3, OLMo 2; Kim et al. 2025) (slide 26) (line_res_gate_both_ends).
Hyper-connections: n learnable lanes with crossovers instead of one fixed lane (Zhu et al. 2025); y = 0.2 x1 + 0.8 x2 scales the gradients (slides 28-29) (line_res_four_lanes, line_knob_board).
Pitfall: multiply mixing weights over many layers and the signal can blow up or die (line_res_snowball, line_whisper_line).
mHC: keep the mixing doubly stochastic (rows and columns sum to 1, entries 0-1); closed under multiplication, so any depth stays stable (Xie et al. 2026) (slides 30-31) (line_res_jugs_glasses).

Her analogy (slide 31): attention = a person listening to others in a meeting (line_round_table); hyper-connections = one person's four clones talking among themselves (line_res_four_clones). Takeaway.
